svg.title: The scenario suite ranks fair policies backwards at H=9 and correctly at H=25 — same positions, same tapes
svg.desc: The scenario suite ranks fair policies backwards at H=9 and correctly at H=25 — same positions, same tapes. finding-10, position mode, K=4 tapes, common random numbers; evidence tier development/pilot. The first category is the PREREGISTERED primary: S9 = +0.6333 over nine policies against the frozen 0.70 pass threshold (p = 0.038) and S6 = -0.2571 over the six fair arms (p = 0.717) — check 1 FAILS; the H=9 run completed 95 of 128 positions under its preregistered 90-minute stop (an unbiased subsample), so the figure plan's '(128 positions)' label for -0.257 was wrong and is corrected here to the record. The second category restricts the SAME 95 positions and tape streams to the seven policies that also ran at H=25 (the two depth-4 arms were omitted at H=25 for cost, so the fair block there is the four cheaper arms): -0.6000 fair / +0.7143 all. The third category is the horizon repair on those same 95 positions: +0.8000 fair / +0.9643 all. The fourth is the full 128-position H=25 arm: +1.0000 / +1.0000 (p = 0.042 for the four fair arms; a monotone n=4 set is a weaker statement than it looks, and whole-game means are not monotone in depth once d4s5 is included). Everything at H=25 is post hoc — designed after the H=9 failure was read; only the direction of the effect was predicted. The +1.000 on 128 positions and +0.800 on the matched 95 differ because d2s7 and d3s5 land 4 points apart on the subset and swap rank (finding-10 section 5 caution 2). Sources: docs/exploratory/finding-10-suite-validation.md.
